audit.whatIsWrong: Full chart read Skill on rows 1, 5 and 6 where the content layer and packet chart read Yasuo.
audit.why: Yasuo's level-2 spike is real — Sweeping Blade at a 0.5s cooldown plus a 4s Steel Tempest gives him a flick-on all-in before your Voidlings exist. First item and beyond, crit plus a 17-21s Wind Wall tip the phases back to him.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 5 and 6 moved to Yasuo with whys rewritten to match.

audit.why: His spikes are level 2, first crit item, and Last Breath dropping from 70s to 30s at rank 3. Yours are level 6 Nether Grasp and Liandry's.
audit.corrected: Last Breath's 30s rank-3 cooldown added where it makes the advice concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit-level asymmetry was asserted in the TL;DR but never carried into the fields that matter: Wind Wall blocks Call of the Void (projectile) but cannot touch Malefic Visions, Voidlings or Nether Grasp, and Last Breath's knock-up is the one thing in his kit that cancels the channel. dosFull[2].d also called Wind Wall a 'fifteen-second' cooldown; it is 25s at rank 1 and 17s maxed.
audit.why: Owner Q is flagged projectile (blockable by Wind Wall-class effects); owner E is targeted and R is a channel flagged interruptible by any CC; enemy R is flagged knockup.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field, dos/donts and the late-game field now state the asymmetry with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit, and the one number the matchup did state (fifteen seconds for Wind Wall) was wrong.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 25s rank 1 / 17s maxed everywhere it appears.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under a shove title; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under an ultimate-usage title; report[7].t made an unsourced 'doubles' claim.
audit.why: Lint findings; bodies contradicted their titles.
audit.corrected: Each rewritten to its own title.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget spell shield (Iron Boundary) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed — it blocks Call of the Void and nothing else you own, so shove and suppress straight through it. - Steel Tempest is 4s, Sweeping Blade 0.5s. - Last Breath falls to 30s at rank 3.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your Q, dashing through the wave onto you, and knocking you out of the channel with Last Breath.

edits.before: Carry by subtraction — every fight starts 4v5 when your R lands; your job is the wave control that makes the fight happen on your timer.
edits.after: Carry by lockdown — Nether Grasp is point-click, so no dash and no wall saves him; make the fight happen while his 30-second R is down.

edits.before: You are a suppression delivery system: shield up, hold a flank, and Grasp their carry the moment the fight breathes. The visions and burn do the rest.
edits.after: Hold Void Shift for his engage and R for his commit — Last Breath at 30 seconds is the only thing in his kit that knocks you out of a channel.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Malefic Visions and Voidlings are not projectiles, so the wall cannot touch them — E a caster, let the wave crash, and shove him off his own tempo.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Wind Wall spent on a minion is a 25-second invitation to walk up and press R.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Last Breath is 30 seconds at rank 3, so he re-enters the fight your R just spent — press it to finish him, never to open.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns every crashed wave into a map play. Cleanse answers the Last Breath knock-up that cancels your channel; Ignite closes R kills.

edits.before: Q online: the silence is your trade answer. Use it on his engage spell, not on poke he can walk around.
edits.after: Yasuo spikes at 2: Sweeping Blade plus a 4-second Q flicks him onto you before your kit is online.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: First item and crit tip it back: Wind Wall eats your Q setup, so bait the 21-second wall before committing.

edits.before: Late Malz is a number: one suppression on their carry equals one won teamfight. Shield up, flank smart, press R.
edits.after: A fed Yasuo walls the peel and Flashes your channel — land R from a flank while his Last Breath is down.

edits.before: Once he has E dash and Q he can flick onto you through the wave and windwall your Q Call of the Void; your answer is W Void Swarm and your passive shield, which absorb his burst and let you E-poke him back so most of this window is a skill trade.
edits.after: With Sweeping Blade at 0.5s and Steel Tempest at 4s he flicks onto you through the wave and walls Call of the Void; your answer is Voidlings and Void Shift, which absorb the burst while Malefic Visions — untouchable by the wall — poke him back, so this window is a skill trade.

edits.before: Use Wind Wall to block your Q and your ranged setup
edits.after: Wall Call of the Void — the only spell you own it can block

edits.before: Level 6 is your moment. Your R is a point-click suppression that ignores every dash and dodge in his kit, so the instant you catch him without Wind Wall you can channel, Zhonya, and delete him before he lands his own knock-up ult. This is exactly why Malzahar is a comfortable Yasuo answer overall — force this window, and use your superior waveclear to shove and roam whenever he can't punish it.
edits.after: Level 6 is your moment. Nether Grasp is point-click, so Sweeping Blade and Wind Wall do nothing to stop it — catch him inside 700 and you channel, Zhonya, and delete him before his own knock-up lands. Only Last Breath, 70 seconds at rank 1, cancels the channel, so press R when it is down. Force this window, and use your waveclear to shove and roam whenever he cannot punish it.

edits.before: The later phases tilt back to him. With crit and mobility online he can windwall your setup, dash through your Voidlings, and flash to dodge your suppress channel, so a fed Yasuo becomes a real threat to your stationary body. Play around your R cooldown, hold your shield for his engage, and rely on team peel — if you land the suppress you win the fight, but if he baits it out you're vulnerable to his all-in.
edits.after: The later phases tilt back to him. With crit online he walls your Q setup, dashes through your Voidlings, and Flashes out of the 700 range your R needs, so a fed Yasuo threatens your stationary body directly. Play around an 80-second R and a 30-second Last Breath, hold Void Shift for his engage, and rely on peel — land the suppression and the fight is over, bait it out and his all-in kills you.

notes: dosFull[2].d shipped a wrong number — it called Wind Wall a fifteen-second cooldown when the kit says 25/23/21/19/17. Corrected. Rows 1, 5 and 6 of the full chart disagreed with the content layer; content already held the correct side on all three, so no win[N] edits were proposed. Not asserted: whether Malzahar's Q silence can stop Sweeping Blade mid-dash, and whether Void Shift's CC immunity prevents the Last Breath knock-up specifically — neither is in the kit text.
